items.title: Show HN: Needle2: 14MB agentic LLM for phones, wearables, smart home and robots
items.raw_content: Hey HN, Henry from Cactus here! We previously released Cactus Needle, a 14MB agentic LLM for tool call, device use, and structured extraction for phones, wearables, smart homes, small robots and microcontrollers. We got really great feedback here, and have now incorporated the suggestions to release Needle 2. The whole model is a single 14MB binary that runs a full session in 28MB of RAM; 45m parameters at 2bit compression. Needle hits 500 tokens/sec decode speed on a Raspberry Pi 5, sits between 400-1,500 tokens/sec on VR devices like Meta Quest 3S and Apple Vision Pro, and ranges 300-700 on sub-$200 phones such as the Samsung A-Series. On the tool call and mobile device use benchmarks, Needle 2 trades wins with closest small models like LFM2.5 230M and Apple Foundation Model, at 5x to 70x smaller, both at f16 vs Needle 2 at 2bit. Needle is based on Simple Attention Networks from our pa
items.title_zh: Show HN：Needle2——面向手机、可穿戴设备、智能家居和机器人的 14MB 智能体 LLM
items.summary: Cactus released Needle 2, a 14MB agentic LLM with 45 million parameters at 2-bit compression that runs a full session in 28MB of RAM. It decodes at 500 tokens per second on a Raspberry Pi 5 and 300–1,500 tokens per second on VR headsets and sub-$200 phones, trading benchmark wins with models such as LFM2.5 230M and Apple's Foundation Model at 5x to 70x their size.

items.title: Show HN: Voice driven murder mystery, Interview AI suspects with your voice
items.raw_content: Hey HN! I'm excited to show off this really fun project I put together. I originally built this project 2-3 years ago, AI was already booming at the time, however voice AI agents were still very early. I loved my proof of concept at the time, but wasn't quite happy with it. I recently had the desire to check out the tech again, and know many of you will be interested. Interviews are speech to speech with OpenAI's gpt-realtime-2.1 over WebRTC. This model is... expensive, and because of that, I have to add some amount of restrictions, conversations are tied to a authenticated Clerk user id. I have also added a 30 minute timer because well, I really don't want to go broke while I sleep tonight. Each suspect has a tool they call when you make a direct accusation. It captures who you accused and a faithful list of the evidence you actually stated. A separate gpt-5-mini judge then decides whic

items.title: Parametron: 50s Japanese computer that uses neither transistors nor vacuum tubes
items.raw_content: The Parametron, a logic element using ferrite cores and parametric oscillation, was invented in 1954 by Eiichi Goto at the University of Tokyo. 4,200 parametrons went into the PC-1, Japan’s first university-built stored-program computer which became the nation's then-fastest in 1958. The parametron’s low cost and electrical stability shaped Japan’s early computer development and scientific research, and nurtured the country's first generation of computer engineers. Science Gallery, 1st floor (ground floor) of Building 1, Faculty of Science, The University of Tokyo. Address; 7-3-1 Hongo, Bunkyo-ku, Tokyo 113-0033 Japan.
items.title_zh: Parametron：不用晶体管也不用真空管的 50 年代日本计算机
items.summary: A historical account describes the Parametron, a logic element using ferrite cores and parametric oscillation that Eiichi Goto invented at the University of Tokyo in 1954. Some 4,200 parametrons went into the PC-1, Japan's first university-built stored-program computer, which became the country's fastest in 1958.

items.title: From Detection to Understanding: TAR and TAR-Bench for Multi-Task Traffic Anomaly Reasoning
items.title_zh: 从检测到理解：面向多任务交通异常推理的 TAR 与 TAR-Bench
items.summary: The authors introduce TAR, a large automatically generated annotation set with chain-of-thought traces for CCTV traffic videos, and TAR-Bench, a smaller human-curated benchmark, covering ten tasks in question answering, temporal reasoning, and scene understanding. Evaluating eleven vision-language models shows a gap between answering questions and reasoning about time or scenes, while supervised fine-tuning on all tasks substantially improves the two models tested.

items.title: Toward a Theory of Value in AI Alignment
items.title_zh: 走向 AI 对齐中的价值理论
items.summary: The authors annotate 94 value alignment papers to surface the implicit theory of values the field relies on, finding that most do not define values and instead substitute preferences, which risks collapsing culturally situated concepts into binary choices. They argue that the shift toward synthetic data and automated raters may foreclose alternative ways of contesting and enacting values in foundation models, and call for making these philosophical commitments explicit.

items.title: Space as an Interventional Invariant: Cross-Modal Predictive Geometry for Stratified Cities and Em-Spaced Intelligence
items.title_zh: 空间作为干预不变量：面向分层城市与具身空间智能的跨模态预测几何
items.summary: The paper defines space as an interventional invariant — the minimal relational structure preserved under admissible actions — and builds a cross-modal predictive geometry combining local state spaces, modality-specific observation maps, an action groupoid, and a predictive-state quotient. Its main result shows identifiability of the latent space up to the centraliser of the intervention group, and the framework is extended to stratified urban systems via sheaf-valued representations and tested in synthetic noisy experiments.

items.title: MRIComp4Flow: Compression of 3D Brain MRI for Training Multi-Modal Generative Models
items.title_zh: MRIComp4Flow：面向多模态生成模型训练的三维脑部 MRI 压缩
items.summary: The study asks whether standard image codecs can compress brain tumor MRI volumes while still supporting training of a 3D generative model, compressing each volume with JPEG2000 or a near-lossless JPEG-LS pipeline before training a Wavelet Flow Matching model conditioned on BraTS sequences. At a 20:1 compression ratio, synthesis quality was statistically equivalent to training on uncompressed data within a pre-specified margin, supporting JPEG2000 as a practical route to scalable 3D MRI generative modeling.

items.title: Site Is Decodable Before Pretraining: Negative Controls for Probing Frozen Brain-MRI Foundation Models
items.title_zh: 站点信息在预训练之前即可解码：探测冻结脑部 MRI 基础模型的阴性对照
items.summary: Probing three frozen 3-D brain-MRI models across two multi-site cohorts shows that acquisition site is far more decodable than any clinical or demographic target, and that untrained models and even 12x12x12 raw voxel inputs predict site nearly as well. The author finds no clinical target where pretraining reliably beats an untrained model, and recommends always reporting untrained-model and raw-input controls alongside probes of brain foundation models.

items.title: Cracks in the Foundation: Seemingly Minor Architectural Choices Impact Long Context Extension
items.title_zh: 地基中的裂缝：看似微小的架构选择会影响长上下文扩展
items.summary: The authors show that four seemingly minor architectural choices — each used by at least one of the Olmo, Llama, or Qwen families — compound to hurt long context extension, with three or more combined dropping downstream performance by up to 47%, an effect invisible in short-context loss. Through controlled ablations varying normalization, GQA, pretraining context length, and sliding window attention, they release OlmPool, a set of 26 comparable 7B models with checkpoints before and after long-context extension.
